title: Stateless MCP Gateways and Registry Admission
service: mcpgateway: a stateless MCP 2026-07-28 gateway in front of scripted in-process backends, with credential mediation, per-caller sliding-window rate limits, a redacting JSONL audit log, a runtime policy engine with a declared failure policy, a request-scoped SSE relay with task routing, and a rebuild of each public call from the audit trail

parts.lesson_anchor: The modern gateway path (steps 1-5); Per-request client capabilities (the gateway is the backend's client); Credential mediation (never pass the outer gateway token to a backend, never reuse a backend token at another issuer or resource); Rate limits without sessions (key by principal, issuer, resource, public tool, cost class and time window; cheap validation before expensive work); code/main.py Gateway.handle, _forward and TokenBucket
planted_bugs: _backend_request spreads the caller's HTTP headers last, so the caller's Authorization (and Mcp-Session-Id, Cookie and the public Mcp-Name) replaces the gateway's backend credential; it surfaces one call away, as the backend's -32001 wrapped by the gateway's result check into a 502 Backend error

_backend_request uses params.setdefault('_meta', ...), which keeps the caller's own _meta, so the backend sees the caller's Tasks declaration and returns a task; it surfaces two steps away, as check_response refusing a result the gateway cannot relay (502)
_admit spends the caller's rate limit from the Mcp-Name routing header before the wire is validated and the policy is asked, so malformed requests drain the quota
RateLimiter.allow rebuilds the whole window with a list comprehension on every call, O(n) per call and quadratic for a busy key
parts.timing_assert: 12,001 allow() calls on one key with a 12,000-call window under 0.05 s. Measured on this machine at load average 6-8: the list version 0.93-1.37 s (18x the limit or more), the deque version 1.5-4.1 ms (12x under it or more)
parts.overfix_guard: the caller's request is left as it was sent; the backend request is compared field by field (a fresh id, the backend tool name, exactly the gateway's three _meta keys with the mediated capabilities) and its headers are exactly the routing headers built from its own params plus the gateway credential; credentials are looked up by (issuer, resource) and a backend without one is never called; an MRTR retry keeps inputResponses and requestState; refused calls spend nothing and a rate-limited call is not forwarded; windows are separate per principal, issuer, tool and cost class, so a global window for speed, one per cost class, the lesson code's principal-only key and a key without the issuer all fail; the lesson's TokenBucket, fixed minute windows, counting refused calls, a strict boundary, the wall clock, checking before pruning, a deque rebuilt by filtering and a bisect that copies the rest are caught

parts.lesson_anchor: Audit the decision chain: request and trace ids, principal and issuer, public tool and backend route, decision and reason, latency and result class, MRTR round or task id; redact bearer tokens, authorization codes, refresh tokens, raw secrets and unnecessary sensitive arguments
parts.storage: an append-only JSONL file, one redacted event per line, flushed per event, with a seq that continues across reopens and counts lines other replicas wrote
parts.exactness: events read back after a reopen equal the redacted events exactly, in write order: JSON-RPC ids 7 and "7" stay distinct, a latency of 0.1 + 0.2 survives, None stays null, non-ASCII text survives, and another replica's line with a raw U+2028 reads back whole

parts.integration: the Part 1 gateway writes into an AuditLog; the file holds no caller token, backend credential or api_key, and reads back as one decision and one result

parts.lesson_anchor: Runtime policy is the primary gateway decision: recomputed for every request from principal, issuer, tenant, name, arguments, admitted pin, backend health, data classification; a Registry record can stay active while a role is revoked; a pinned descriptor does not stop a destination crossing a tenant boundary; incident policy can quarantine state changes; no allow decision cached under a connection or session; fail closed for state changes and sensitive reads, a short-lived last-known policy only for explicitly approved public reads; record the policy version and failure path; MRTR through a gateway (re-authorize every retry)

deviations: Part 1: the suggested defect order was _meta, token, rate limit, timing. The fake backend checks its credential before it reads the request, so the token defect surfaces first (a 502 carrying the backend's -32001) and the _meta defect second (the backend returns a task because it saw the caller's Tasks declaration, and the gateway's result check refuses it). The token defect is the caller's headers merged over the gateway's; handle receives the HTTP headers, Authorization included, instead of a separate bearer argument, so the outer token can actually leak.

Part 1: the suggested limiter was a TokenBucket keeping a timestamp list. The lesson's sentence is 'Key limits by ... and time window', and a timestamp list is a sliding-window log, so the exam's RateLimiter is a sliding window with the lesson's key; the lesson's TokenBucket semantics are one of the wrong fixes. The suggested 50,000 calls take about 4 s quadratic on this machine, over the 3 s cap, so the timing case is 12,001 calls on one key with a 12,000-call window (about 1 s against 2 ms).

Part 1: the early spend is keyed off the Mcp-Name routing header, the shortcut the lesson's header routing invites. Besides the suggested global-bucket guard, the test checks that policy-refused calls are 403 every time and that a rate-limited call is not forwarded, which fixes the place of the spend between the policy and the forward.

Part 2: the log numbers events with seq (continuing across reopens and counting other replicas' lines) so Part 5 has a tie-breaker. Redaction is by key name under arguments and inputResponses, plus header names only; the gateway never puts requestState itself into an event, only a digest.

Part 3: roles come from the policy document keyed by (issuer, principal); CallContext.token_roles is a distractor, because a token outlives a revocation. 'Do not cache an allow decision per session' is tested as 'a revocation applies to the next decision'. The descriptor pin, admission and health are boolean inputs, since pins and registry admission belong to lessons 15 and 30.

Part 4: backends hand the relay parsed JSON-RPC messages (SSE decoding is lesson 09's Part 5) and the relay writes client-side SSE. The gateway gives the backend its own progress token, the backend request id, so 'id rewriting must not touch progressToken' becomes two separate mappings (token to the client's token, id to the client's id). requestState is an opaque string, so 'not re-serialized' is tested as the result passing through untouched apart from _meta, plus the backend's HMAC check on the retry. 'Task routes kept until the terminal state' is tested as routes surviving the stream's close; the route table has no expiry here.

Part 5: two event kinds, decision and result, with the identity (issuer, principal, trace_id, request_id). MRTR rounds link through state digests (state_in to an earlier state_out) because the retry has a new id and the gateway cannot read requestState; task requests link through (issuer, principal, taskId) to the result that returned the task.

Facts used beyond docs/en.md: the progress notification params (as in lesson 29's code) and the request's params._meta.progressToken (the MCP progress utility); task fields, the -32602 for an unknown task id and ownership checks (lesson 13); inputRequests and the elicitation, sampling and roots capability names (lessons 11 and 12); traceparent in _meta (lesson 20); -32001, -32003 and -32029 (this lesson's code/main.py). The -32603 and HTTP 502 for backend failures, the audit event fields and the SECRET_KEYS list are this gateway's own choices, stated in its docstrings.
